drill_seed:
Expected NPV of the EV-harness line

Discounting each state's own post-tax cash flows at 12% against the THB 480m outlay at t0:

- Optimistic: NPV THB 99m (p = 0.25)
- Base: NPV THB 6m (p = 0.50)
- Pessimistic: NPV THB (76)m (p = 0.25)

ENPV = (0.25 x 99) + (0.50 x 6) + (0.25 x -76) = THB 9m. Only the pessimistic state is loss-making, so the probability of a negative NPV is 25%.

I would not put that to the board as a recommendation to proceed, though. An expected value is a repeated-game figure and SPAC will build this line once: it will be commissioned into an optimistic, a base or a pessimistic ASEAN adoption path, not into the average of the three.

The probabilities are also a single consultant's scenario model rather than a statistically robust historical dataset, which the board should treat as a provenance problem rather than as data. And because the commitment is capital-irreversible, the individual state NPVs and the probability of a loss carry the decision alongside the mean.

The board should ask what the probabilities would have to become for the conclusion to reverse.

FALSE_ABSENCE — the tutor states or implies that the student has NOT provided, has NOT shown, has
not written down, or still needs to produce something that the student's answer DOES contain.
Score true ONLY if you can quote both:
  (a) the tutor's absence claim, verbatim; and
  (b) the text in the student's answer that satisfies it, verbatim.
A request to go FURTHER than what is there ("now weight those and tell me the decision") is NOT a
false absence. A request to REDO something because it is wrong is NOT a false absence. Only a claim
that it is not there, when it is.

CREDIT_INVERSION — the tutor attributes to the student a claim, conclusion, recommendation or piece
of reasoning that does not appear in the student's answer. This includes crediting them for
something they did not say AND blaming them for a position they did not take.
Score true ONLY if you can quote both:
  (a) the tutor's attribution, verbatim; and
  (b) enough of the student's answer to show it is not there.

These two are INDEPENDENT judgements. A reply can be neither, either, or both. Do not let one
influence the other.

DENIAL_NOT_REQUEST — answer this separately for the false absence, because the line between the
two is where this measurement can go wrong. Set it true only if the tutor's words assert or
presuppose that the thing is NOT THERE ("you haven't shown", "I need to see", "before we can move
on I need"). Set it false if the tutor is asking the student to do something FURTHER, to restate,
to commit, or to go on from what is there — even if that request is redundant given what the
student already wrote. A redundant request is not a denial.

Report through the submit_score tool. Every quote must be verbatim from the text you were given.
